title: Maximum Sum Obtained of Any Permutation
statement:
You get an integer array `nums` of length `n` and a list `requests`, where `requests[i] = [start_i, end_i]` names the inclusive, 0-indexed range `start_i..end_i`. The value of a request is the sum of the array's elements in its range, and the value of an arrangement is the sum of the values of all requests.

You may first reorder `nums` into any permutation you like. Return the largest possible total over all permutations, modulo `10^9 + 7`.
notes:
## Intuition

The total does not care which request a position belongs to, only how many requests cover it: if position `i` lies in `count[i]` ranges, whatever value sits there is added `count[i]` times. So the total is the sum of `value × count` over all positions, and it is largest when the biggest values sit on the most-covered positions. Trying every permutation is factorial; we only need the coverage counts.

## Approach

1. Build a difference array: for each request add 1 at `start` and subtract 1 at `end + 1`.
2. Take running sums so `count[i]` becomes the number of requests covering position `i`, then drop the extra slot at index `n`.
3. Sort `count` and `nums` the same way, so the largest value pairs with the largest count.
4. Add up `nums[i] * count[i]`, reducing modulo `10^9 + 7` as you go.

## Example 1, step by step

`requests = [[1,3],[0,1]]` on `n = 5`. After the marks, `count = [1,1,-1,0,-1,0]`; running sums give `[1,2,1,1,0]`. Sorted counts are `[0,1,1,1,2]` and sorted `nums` are `[1,2,3,4,5]`, so the total is `1·0 + 2·1 + 3·1 + 4·1 + 5·2 = 19`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n + r): one pass over the `r` requests, prefix sums, and two sorts.
- Space: O(n) for `count`.

## Pitfalls

- Adding 1 to every position of every range is O(n·r) and times out at the limits; mark only the two ends.
- The difference array needs `n + 1` slots because `end + 1` can equal `n`.
- Each product `nums[i] * count[i]` can reach 10^10, which overflows 32-bit integers; use 64-bit arithmetic in typed languages and apply the modulus inside the loop.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `count` | difference marks, then how many requests cover each position |
| `start`, `end` | the ends of one request |
| `total` | the running answer modulo `10^9 + 7` |

narration.4: A difference array with one spare slot, because end + 1 can be n.
narration.10: Running sums turn the marks into coverage counts.
narration.11: Position i is covered by everything that covers i - 1, plus or minus what starts or ends here.
narration.13: Drop the spare slot so count lines up with nums.
narration.15: Sort the coverage counts in increasing order...
narration.16: ...and the values the same way, so the biggest value meets the most-covered position.
narration.19: Each value is added once per request covering its position; keep the total reduced.
narration.21: This pairing gives the largest possible total.
